the latency insensitive systems theory is a promising approach for the design of SoC. The main benefit is to preserve the IP performances when encapsulation.
A new synchronization wrapper model is proposed to optimize the performances of IPs encapsulated into a latency insensitive system context.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of an optimized latency insensitive system context for DVB-DSNG modem IP encapsulation.
a new methodology of SoC design based on the LIS theory.
the following questions: How to design a synchronization processor? How to optimize it in terms of speed and area? How to synthesize it? How to integrate it in a LIS context?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our contribution is a new IP wrapper model that is able to encapsulate an IP with its interconnection into a LIS wrapper, and to optimize the synchronization processor to meet timing and area constraints.
the methodology and tool chain proposed in this paper is a promising solution for the development of SoC based on high level synthesis and latency insensitive systems.
our approach has been validated by the design and synthesis of the DVB-DSNG modem IP, which is part of a SoC design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an efficient solution for the synchronization of IPs with a latency insensitive system context.
the LIS theory has been extended to the design of high level synthesizable synchronous IPs.
we are able to design a DVB-DSNG modem with a 2.2Gbps data throughput, a 3ms end to end latency and a 1W power consumption in a 90nm technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the LIS theory could be used to design and synthesize a synchronization processor in a SoC context.
the LIS approach can be successfully combined with HLS.
the latency insensitive system theory can be used in the high-level synthesis context.
